name: Apple Inc.
description: Designs and sells consumer electronics, including the iPhone, Mac, and iPad, along with related software and services. Purchases semiconductor chips and device assembly services from contract manufacturers; sells finished devices directly to consumers and through retail partners.

name: Microsoft Corporation
description: Develops software, cloud computing services (Azure), and hardware including Surface devices and Xbox consoles. Purchases server hardware and semiconductor chips from technology suppliers; sells cloud and software services to businesses and consumers.

name: NVIDIA Corporation
description: Designs graphics processing units (GPUs) and AI accelerator chips, manufactured under contract by semiconductor foundries. Sells chips primarily to cloud computing providers and data center operators building AI infrastructure.

name: Exxon Mobil Corporation
description: Explores for, produces, and refines oil and natural gas. Purchases drilling and oilfield services from specialized service providers; sells refined fuel products to transportation companies, airlines, and fuel distributors.

name: Chevron Corporation
description: Integrated oil and gas company engaged in exploration, production, and refining. Purchases oilfield equipment and services from energy service companies; sells fuel and petrochemical products to transportation and industrial customers.

name: ConocoPhillips
description: Independent exploration and production company focused on oil and natural gas extraction. Purchases drilling equipment and well services from oilfield service providers; sells crude oil and natural gas to refiners and energy marketers.

name: American Airlines Group Inc.
description: Operates a major U.S. passenger airline offering domestic and international routes. Purchases aircraft from commercial aircraft manufacturers and jet fuel from energy companies; sells air travel to consumers and corporate accounts.

name: Delta Air Lines Inc.
description: Operates a major U.S. passenger airline with an extensive domestic and international network. Purchases aircraft from commercial aircraft manufacturers and jet fuel from energy companies; sells air travel to consumers and corporate clients.

name: United Continental Holdings Inc.
description: Parent company of United Airlines, a major U.S. passenger carrier. Purchases aircraft from commercial aircraft manufacturers and jet fuel from energy companies; sells air travel to consumers and business travelers.

name: Johnson & Johnson
description: Develops and manufactures pharmaceuticals and medical devices. Purchases active ingredients and manufacturing services from contract manufacturers and life sciences suppliers; sells products to hospitals, pharmacies, and drug distributors.

name: Pfizer Inc.
description: Develops, manufactures, and markets pharmaceuticals and vaccines. Purchases active ingredients and lab/manufacturing services from contract manufacturers; sells medicines primarily through large pharmaceutical distributors.

name: Merck & Co. Inc.
description: Develops pharmaceuticals, vaccines, and animal health products. Purchases specialized manufacturing and lab services from contract development organizations; sells products through major pharmaceutical distributors.

name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
description: Global bank offering consumer banking, commercial lending, and investment banking services. Purchases payment processing and technology services from financial infrastructure providers; serves individual, corporate, and institutional clients.

name: Bank of America Corp.
description: Major U.S. bank providing retail banking, wealth management, and institutional financial services. Purchases payment network and technology services from financial infrastructure providers; serves consumer and business banking clients.

name: Citigroup Inc.
description: Global bank offering consumer and institutional banking services across multiple countries. Purchases technology consulting and IT infrastructure services from professional services firms; serves retail and corporate banking clients.

name: Procter & Gamble Co.
description: Manufactures household and personal care products sold under brands including Tide, Gillette, and Pampers. Purchases raw chemical ingredients and packaging materials from chemical and materials suppliers; sells products through large retail chains.

name: The Coca-Cola Company
description: Manufactures beverage concentrate and syrup, distributed and bottled through franchise partners. Purchases sweeteners and packaging materials from ingredient suppliers; sells finished beverages through retail chains and food service partners.

name: PepsiCo Inc.
description: Manufactures beverages and snack foods including Pepsi, Lay's, and Gatorade. Purchases agricultural ingredients and packaging materials from food suppliers; sells products through large retail and warehouse club chains.

name: General Motors Co.
description: Manufactures and sells automobiles under brands including Chevrolet, GMC, and Cadillac. Purchases engines, electronics, and body components from automotive parts suppliers; sells vehicles through dealer networks and to fleet/rental customers.

name: Ford Motor Company
description: Manufactures and sells automobiles and trucks including the F-150 pickup. Purchases braking systems, electronics, and body components from automotive parts suppliers; sells vehicles through dealer networks and to fleet/rental customers.

name: Tesla Inc.
description: Designs and manufactures electric vehicles and energy storage systems. Purchases battery cells and raw battery materials from battery manufacturers; sells vehicles directly to consumers rather than through independent dealers.

name: Walmart Inc.
description: Operates a global chain of discount department stores and warehouse clubs. Purchases consumer packaged goods, groceries, and general merchandise from a broad range of manufacturers; sells products directly to consumers.

name: Costco Wholesale Corporation
description: Operates membership-based warehouse retail clubs selling groceries and general merchandise in bulk. Purchases consumer packaged goods from manufacturers at large volumes; sells products to paying members.

name: Target Corporation
description: Operates a chain of general merchandise discount stores. Purchases consumer packaged goods and general merchandise from a broad range of manufacturers; sells products directly to consumers.

name: AT&T Inc.
description: Provides wireless, broadband, and telecommunications services. Purchases network equipment and infrastructure from telecom equipment manufacturers; sells communication services directly to consumers and businesses.

name: Verizon Communications Inc.
description: Provides wireless communications and broadband internet services. Purchases network equipment from telecom infrastructure manufacturers; sells communication services to consumers and enterprise customers.

name: T-Mobile US Inc.
description: Provides wireless communications services across the United States. Purchases network equipment from telecom infrastructure manufacturers; sells mobile service plans directly to consumers and businesses.

name: Boeing Company
description: Designs and manufactures commercial passenger aircraft and defense systems. Sells aircraft primarily to airlines and aircraft leasing companies; sources major structural components, engines, and avionics from specialized aerospace suppliers.

name: Lockheed Martin Corporation
description: Designs and manufactures aerospace and defense systems, primarily for government and military customers. Purchases specialized defense components and electronics from aerospace suppliers; sells systems mainly to government defense agencies.

name: GE Aerospace
description: Designs and manufactures jet engines for commercial and military aircraft. Purchases specialized alloys and precision components from aerospace parts suppliers; sells engines to aircraft manufacturers and airlines for maintenance.

name: TSMC
description: Manufactures semiconductor chips on contract for other companies (a 'foundry' model). Purchases silicon wafers and lithography equipment from semiconductor equipment suppliers; sells chip manufacturing capacity to technology and hardware companies that design their own chips.

name: Foxconn
description: Provides electronics manufacturing and assembly services on contract for other companies. Purchases electronic components from a wide supplier base; sells assembly and manufacturing services to consumer electronics brands.

name: Spirit AeroSystems
description: Manufactures aircraft structures, including fuselages, for commercial aircraft manufacturers. Purchases aerospace-grade metals and composite materials from materials suppliers; sells structural assemblies to aircraft manufacturers.

name: Honeywell International
description: Manufactures avionics, aircraft systems, and industrial control technologies. Purchases electronic components and specialized materials from industrial suppliers; sells aerospace systems to aircraft manufacturers and industrial equipment across sectors.

name: Airbus SE
description: Designs and manufactures commercial passenger aircraft, competing directly with Boeing. Sells aircraft primarily to airlines and leasing companies; sources structural components and engines from aerospace suppliers.
